transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because flying has started to feel... way scarier than it really should. 

Just the idea of getting on a plane makes me... I just keep picturing that turbulence from my honeymoon flight again. Even though I know people fly safely every day, it's just... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Is it just flying that makes you feel scared or anxious, or are there other situations that trigger similar feelings for you?
Um... no, not really. Just... just the flying. I mean, other things are fine. It's really just getting on a plane.
When did you first start feeling this excessive fear of flying?
Um... well, it started after that flight I mentioned. The one coming back from my honeymoon. So... I guess it's been about two years and five months now.
Have you been avoiding flying since this fear started?

Um... yeah. I try not to. I usually just choose to drive, even if it's a really long way. Or... I'll just turn down trainings for work. And if we absolutely have to even talk about a trip, I kind of... I need my husband sitting there with me. Just to get through talking about it without backing out.
How would you rate your level of fear when you think about flying, on a scale from 1 to 10?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't know if I can put a number on it. It's just... I'd rather not do it.
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with friends or family in any way?

Um... not really, I guess. I mean, I'm still managing my home life and my job just fine. It mostly just... pushes back personal plans. Like, there was this trip to Florence we were supposed to take, and I just keep putting it off. And... well, I guess at work, I've been passing up some conferences and trainings my supervisor thinks would be good for me. But... yeah, otherwise things are mostly normal.
Do you experience any physical symptoms, such as a racing heart or sweating, when you think about flying?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Like... if I'm trying to look at flights for a conference, or... even just hearing a plane overhead... my chest gets tight right away. I just... I get this rush of panic. It makes me just want to shut my laptop or... just get away from the thought entirely. So... yeah.
Does thinking about flying interfere with your daily activities when you're not actually planning a trip?
Um... no, not really. If I don't have to think about it, I... I just don't. It doesn't really come up unless I'm supposed to go somewhere.
Do you ever have periods where your fear of flying seems to lessen or fade away?
Um... I don't think so. It's pretty much just... always the same. If I have to think about getting on a plane, the feeling is just there. I haven't really noticed it ever going away.
Do you feel like your fear of flying is causing you a lot of distress?

Um... I guess so. I mean, I'm still managing my job and home life fine. But... I don't know, I've started passing up some trainings and conferences that my supervisor thinks would help me grow. And... it keeps pushing back personal plans. Like this trip to Florence I was really excited about. So... yeah, it bothers me.
Have you had to turn down any social invitations because they involved flying?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean, mostly I just... I choose to drive instead, even if it's really far. Or I just turn down those work trainings. And... if we do have to talk about planning a trip or something, I... I make my husband sit with me. Just so I don't back out.
Is your fear of flying usually triggered by a specific thought, object, or situation, like seeing a plane or talking about flying?

Um... yeah, I guess. Like... if I'm looking at flights online for one of those conferences, or... even if I just hear a plane overhead outside. My chest kind of... it tightens up right away. And I get this... I don't know, this rush of panic. I just feel like I need to shut the laptop or... just get away from the thought of it.
Has your fear of flying affected your performance at work or impacted your ability to fulfill your job responsibilities?

Um... well, like I said earlier... I'm still doing okay with my actual job duties. But... I guess it is affecting things a little, since I keep turning down those trainings and conferences my supervisor suggests. So... yeah, I'm missing out on things that would help me advance.
Are there any aspects of your daily life, outside of flying or planning trips, where you feel your fear of flying is having a direct impact?
Um... no, not really. Just the trips and the work stuff. Everything else is... fine, I guess. My day-to-day life is pretty normal.
